Stage 3 · Grammar

Grammar

I'm a teacher · I'm an engineer
a + consonant soundan + vowel sound
a teacheran engineer
a doctoran artist
a nursean office worker
  • Jobs take a or an: I'm a teacher. She's a doctor.
  • Use an before a vowel sound (a, e, i, o, u): an engineer, an artist, an office worker.
  • Ask: What do you do? — I'm a nurse. / What's your job? — I'm a chef.

→ Present Simple (I work / she works) comes fully in Lesson 9.

🔧 Build it yourself
  • 🔧 Build it yourself
  • Build it: teacher → A teacher. Vowel sound? → AN engineer, AN artist.
  • ⚠ Russian and Kazakh have no a/an — but every English job needs one: I'm A nurse (я медсестра).

Stage 6 · Speaking

Your turn

Write two short lines: your job, and ask a question.

When you finish, open the model answer and check yourself.

Model answer

I'm a student. I work in a school. What do you do?

Check yourself:

  • Did you use I'm a / an + job?
  • Did you choose the right a / an?
  • Did you ask What do you do? / What's your job?
Talk to Sam. Answer with the words from this lesson.

Read each message. Tap 🔊 to hear Sam.

Sam

Hi again! I'm Sam. 👋

Sam

What do you do?

Sam

Nice! 😊

Sam

What's your friend's job?

Sam

Cool! 🎨

Sam

Listen: “My friend is engineer.” 🤔

Why

Jobs need a or an: My friend is an engineer. Use an before a vowel sound.

Sam

Yes! “My friend is an engineer.” Great catch. 🌟

Feedback

Well done: you said your job and fixed a / an. Next time, say it out loud too.
